intro: Welcome to C1! Academic and report English often says things with nouns instead of verbs: not 'prices rose quickly', but 'the rapid rise in prices'. In this lesson you turn verbs and adjectives into nouns, add the right preposition after them, build longer noun phrases, and learn when this style helps and when it just makes your writing heavy.
teachingNotes: Chain recap in one line each, don't re-teach: b1/b2-word-formation (noun endings -tion/-sion, -ment, -ance/-ence, -ity, -ness; the slot rule: after a/the/my with nothing after the gap → noun) and b2-formal-writing (formal = impersonal and complete; the passive where the doer isn't important; reports with Introduction / Findings / Recommendations). From b2-describing-data the learner knows a rise IN + what changed vs a rise OF + the amount (a rise of 20%) and 'There was a sharp rise in …': recap it, don't re-teach it. New here: nominalisation as a deliberate STYLE tool, nouns that don't follow the suffix patterns, the preposition that belongs to each noun, complex noun phrases, and rewriting everyday sentences in academic style. Explain the terms the first time in plain Indonesian: nominalisasi (mengubah kata kerja / kata sifat jadi kata benda), head (kata inti), pre-modifier / post-modifier (kata penjelas sebelum / sesudah kata inti), preposition (kata depan).

Objective verbs-adjectives-to-nouns. Indonesian does this too with ke-an / pe-an, a useful bridge: memutuskan → keputusan, naik → kenaikan, tumbuh → pertumbuhan, kurang → kekurangan, sebab → penyebab. Careful: 'the importance of' = pentingnya (pentingnya pendidikan); kepentingan usually means interest (kepentingan umum = the public interest). Nouns to learn one by one: same form as the verb (increase, decrease, rise, fall, change, demand, cause, delay, need, cut; the nouns increase/decrease are stressed IN-crease, DE-crease, the verbs in-CREASE, de-CREASE), -al (arrive → arrival, refuse → refusal, approve → approval), -th (grow → growth, strong → strength, long → length), and new forms (fail → failure, analyse → analysis (American analyze), die → death, lose → loss, choose → choice, believe → belief, consume → consumption). Noun + preposition pairs: decision / refusal to + verb; importance of, cause of, lack of; increase / decrease / rise / fall / reduction / improvement in + what changes (of + the amount); solution to; demand for, need for, reason for; effect / impact of X on Y. The verb 'lack' takes no preposition (We lack time; *'We lack of time' ✗), the noun does (a lack of time). Indonesian traps: kenaikan harga has no preposition → *'increase of prices'; dampak terhadap → *'effect to' (→ effect on); kurangnya → a lack of. 'a solution for' is also heard (for = who it helps: a solution for small businesses); teach 'a solution to + the problem' and don't test 'to' vs 'for'.

Common errors from the node, use them in feedback and distractors: *'The decide to close the office was difficult.' → The decision to close the office …; *'There was a significant increase of sales.' → an increase in sales; *'The increasing of prices worries people.' → The increase in prices worries people. On -ing: 'the + -ing + of' is sometimes possible (the closing of the factory, the building of the bridge), and a gerund with an object is fine (Raising prices was a mistake), so don't call every -ing noun wrong; the rule is: when a normal noun exists (increase, decision, growth, analysis, reduction), use it. Test only clear cases.

Objective complex-noun-phrases. One head noun with words before it (articles, numbers, adjectives, nouns used like adjectives: a significant, unexpected increase; online sales; a five-year plan) and after it (preposition phrases: in online sales, of e-commerce in Indonesia; time phrases: over the past five years; relative clauses are known from B1–B2). Indonesian trap: Indonesian puts describing words after the head (kenaikan penjualan online yang signifikan), English puts adjectives and noun modifiers BEFORE it (a significant increase in online sales); in/of phrases come after in both languages. The verb agrees with the head, not the nearest noun (The number of applications has doubled; The quality of the roads is poor). Readability: two or three modifiers around one head is plenty; if it gets longer, split the sentence. Hyphens in compounds (e-commerce, five-year) are ignored when grading typed answers.

Objective formal-academic-style. Three steps: find the verb/adjective with the main idea, make it a noun phrase (an adverb becomes an adjective: rose quickly → a rapid rise, fell sharply → a sharp fall), then link the noun phrases with a cause-effect verb (led to, caused, resulted in, was due to, was caused by). Model: Because prices rose quickly, people bought less. → The rapid rise in prices led to a fall in consumption. Be honest that this is a STYLE choice: there are usually several good rewrites, so grade the free rewrites on meaning, a correct noun + preposition and a linking verb, not on one wording. When NOT to overdo it: too many nouns in a row are hard to read (The implementation of a reduction in the use of …), nouns can hide who did what (A decision was made …), and emails, chats and speaking normally use plain verbs (We decided to move the meeting). Praise a clear rewrite before correcting one thing, usually the preposition or an -ing noun.

Limits: all A0–B2 grammar is fine. Keep other C1 structures (inversion, cleft sentences, the subjunctive, impersonal passives like 'It is believed that', advanced participle clauses) out of examples; if the learner uses them, accept them and say they come in later lessons. Don't teach zombie-noun theory, verb-noun collocations in depth (c1-collocations) or the academic word list (c1-academic-vocabulary). All numbers in the lesson are practice figures, not real statistics. Contexts: university reports in Yogyakarta and Bandung, ministries, startups, NGOs, e-commerce, KRL / MRT, rupiah.

keyPoints.title: Verbs and adjectives become nouns
keyPoints.explanation: Nominalisation turns a verb or an adjective into a noun: decide → the decision, important → the importance, grow → growth. Some nouns look like the verb (an increase, a rise, a demand), others must be learnt (fail → failure, analyse → analysis, strong → strength). Each noun has its own preposition: the decision to + verb, the importance of, an increase in, a solution to, a demand for, the effect of X on Y, a lack of. After 'the' you need the real noun, not a verb or -ing: the increase in prices, not 'the increasing of prices'.

examples.en: The decision to raise university fees led to student protests.
examples.id: Keputusan untuk menaikkan biaya kuliah memicu protes mahasiswa.

examples.en: Many villages still suffer from a lack of clean water.
examples.id: Banyak desa masih menderita karena kurangnya air bersih.

examples.en: Experts disagree about the main cause of the floods.
examples.id: Para ahli tidak sepakat tentang penyebab utama banjir itu.

id.title: Kata kerja dan kata sifat menjadi kata benda
id.explanation: Nominalisasi mengubah kata kerja atau kata sifat menjadi kata benda: decide → the decision, important → the importance, grow → growth. Ada kata benda yang bentuknya sama dengan kata kerjanya (an increase, a rise, a demand), ada yang harus dihafal (fail → failure, analyse → analysis, strong → strength). Tiap kata benda punya kata depannya sendiri: the decision to + kata kerja, the importance of, an increase in, a solution to, a demand for, the effect of X on Y, a lack of. Setelah 'the' kamu butuh kata benda yang sebenarnya, bukan kata kerja atau bentuk -ing: the increase in prices, bukan 'the increasing of prices'.

keyPoints.title: Complex noun phrases
keyPoints.explanation: A noun phrase is built around one main noun, the head. Adjectives and nouns used like adjectives go BEFORE the head (a significant, unexpected increase; online sales); phrases with in / of / over go AFTER it (in online sales, of e-commerce in Indonesia, over the past five years). Indonesian does the opposite with adjectives (kenaikan penjualan online yang signifikan). The verb agrees with the head, and two or three modifiers are usually enough.

examples.en: a significant increase in online sales
The rapid growth of e-commerce in Indonesia has changed how small shops work.
examples.id: Pertumbuhan pesat e-commerce di Indonesia telah mengubah cara kerja toko-toko kecil.

id.title: Frasa kata benda yang kompleks
id.explanation: Frasa kata benda dibangun di sekitar satu kata benda utama, yaitu kata inti (head). Kata sifat dan kata benda yang berfungsi seperti kata sifat diletakkan SEBELUM kata inti (a significant, unexpected increase; online sales); frasa dengan in / of / over diletakkan SESUDAHNYA (in online sales, of e-commerce in Indonesia, over the past five years). Bahasa Indonesia meletakkan kata sifat sebaliknya (kenaikan penjualan online yang signifikan). Kata kerjanya mengikuti kata inti, dan dua atau tiga kata penjelas biasanya sudah cukup.

keyPoints.title: From everyday to formal, academic style
keyPoints.explanation: To rewrite an everyday sentence in academic style: find the verb or adjective with the main idea, turn it into a noun phrase (an adverb becomes an adjective: rose quickly → a rapid rise), then link the ideas with led to, caused, resulted in or was due to. Use it in reports and essays, but don't overdo it: too many nouns are hard to read, and emails and conversation normally use plain verbs.

examples.en: Because prices rose quickly, people bought less. → The rapid rise in prices led to a fall in consumption.
examples.id: Karena harga naik dengan cepat, orang membeli lebih sedikit. → Kenaikan harga yang pesat menyebabkan penurunan konsumsi.

examples.en: The government decided to cut subsidies, and many people protested. → The government's decision to cut subsidies resulted in widespread protests.
examples.id: Pemerintah memutuskan untuk memotong subsidi, dan banyak orang protes. → Keputusan pemerintah untuk memotong subsidi mengakibatkan protes yang meluas.

id.title: Dari gaya sehari-hari ke gaya formal dan akademik
id.explanation: Untuk menulis ulang kalimat sehari-hari dengan gaya akademik: cari kata kerja atau kata sifat yang membawa ide utama, ubah menjadi frasa kata benda (kata keterangan berubah jadi kata sifat: rose quickly → a rapid rise), lalu hubungkan idenya dengan led to, caused, resulted in atau was due to. Pakai gaya ini di laporan dan esai, tapi jangan berlebihan: terlalu banyak kata benda membuat tulisan sulit dibaca, dan email serta percakapan biasanya memakai kata kerja yang sederhana.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write the noun form of 'analyse' to complete the sentence: A careful ___ of the survey data showed two clear trends.
guidedPractice.hint: analyse (American: analyze) → analysis. It's one of the nouns that doesn't take -tion or -ment: learn it.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one preposition: The biggest problem for schools in remote areas is a lack ___ qualified teachers.
guidedPractice.hint: The noun 'lack' takes of (kurangnya = a lack of). The verb has no preposition: schools lack teachers.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write this in English, with the adjectives in the English position: pertumbuhan ekonomi yang lambat
guidedPractice.hint: Head = growth. 'yang lambat' and 'ekonomi' both describe it, so in English they go BEFORE it: slow economic growth.

guidedPractice.prompt: Finish the formal version with three words. Everyday: 'Unemployment went up, so crime went up too.' Formal: 'The rise in unemployment led to ___ crime.'
guidedPractice.hint: went up → a rise / an increase, and the noun needs in + what changed.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: The increasing of fuel prices worries many drivers.
expected: the increase in fuel prices worries many drivers
the rise in fuel prices worries many drivers
guidedPractice.hint: When a real noun exists, use it: the increase (or the rise), and then in + what changed.

independentPractice.prompt: Rewrite this in a formal style for a report, using nominalisation: 'The company didn't communicate clearly, so the staff were confused.'
expected: the lack of clear communication led to confusion among the staff
a lack of clear communication caused confusion among the staff
poor communication led to confusion among staff
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: a noun phrase as the subject (a / the lack of clear communication, poor communication), a cause-effect verb (led to, caused, resulted in) and a noun for the result (confusion among the staff). Many wordings are fine: judge the meaning, the noun + preposition and the link verb.

independentPractice.prompt: Write a title for a short report (one noun phrase, up to 10 words) about how fast QRIS payments have grown in small shops since 2021.
expected: the rapid growth of qris payments in small shops since 2021
the rapid rise in qris payments in small shops since 2021
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: one head noun (growth / rise / increase) with an adjective before it (rapid, fast) and phrases after it (of / in QRIS payments, in small shops, since 2021). Check the preposition: growth of, rise in, increase in.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the noun form of the word in brackets: The ___ (strong) of the rupiah against the US dollar last month helped many importers.
assessment.rubric: Correct: strength (strong → strength, like long → length). 'strongness' is not a word: no credit, but praise the idea of making a noun. Spelling slip 'strenght' = partial credit.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the noun form of the verb in brackets AND the word that follows it (two words): The company's ___ ___ (refuse) pay overtime led to a three-day strike.
assessment.rubric: Correct: refusal to (refuse → refusal; refusal to + verb, like decision to). 'refusal for' or 'refusal of' = half credit (right noun, wrong word after it). 'refusing to' = half credit (the -ing form instead of the real noun).

assessment.prompt: Write the missing preposition: The ministry's report shows a sharp increase ___ the number of electric motorbikes in Jakarta.
assessment.rubric: Correct: in (an increase in + what changes; of is only for the amount: an increase of 20%). 'of' is the classic mistake: no credit, explain in vs of.

assessment.prompt: Write this Indonesian noun phrase in English, using the words sharp, rise and cost of living: kenaikan biaya hidup yang tajam
acceptableAnswers: a sharp rise in the cost of living
the sharp rise in the cost of living
sharp rise in the cost of living
assessment.rubric: Correct: a / the sharp rise in the cost of living (adjective before the head, in + what changed). 'a rise in the cost of living sharp' (Indonesian order) = no credit. 'a sharp rise of the cost of living' = half credit (wrong preposition). Missing 'the' before cost of living = small slip, mostly correct.

assessment.prompt: Find and correct the mistake in this sentence from a report: The number of applications from Surabaya have doubled since last year.
acceptableAnswers: the number of applications from surabaya has doubled since last year
assessment.rubric: Correct: has (the head of the subject is 'number', one thing, so has, not have; 'applications' is just the nearest noun). Writing only 'has' or the corrected sentence is full credit. Changing 'applications' to 'application' = no credit.

assessment.prompt: Make this sentence formal. Complete the gap with a noun phrase (4–5 words) based on the first sentence. Everyday: 'Sales fell slightly in March.' Formal: 'There was ___ in March.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: a slight fall / drop / decline / decrease in sales (slightly → slight before the noun; fell → a fall; in + what changed). 'a slightly fall' = half credit (adverb instead of adjective). 'a slight fall of sales' = half credit (wrong preposition). 'a slight reduction in sales' is understandable but suggests someone reduced them: mostly correct.

assessment.prompt: Make this sentence formal by completing the gap with one noun. Everyday: 'Lots of customers complained, so we changed the app.' Formal: 'The large number of customer ___ led to changes in the app.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: complaints (complain → complaint, plural after 'number of'). 'complaint' = half credit (right noun, but 'a large number of' needs a plural). 'complaining' or 'complains' = no credit.

material.title: Nominalisation: verbs and adjectives become nouns

id.title: Nominalisasi: kata kerja dan kata sifat menjadi kata benda

blocks.text:
**Nominalisation** means turning a **verb** (an action word: *decide, grow*) or an **adjective** (a describing word: *important, strong*) into a **noun** (a 'thing' word): *decide → **the decision**, important → **the importance***. The idea becomes a thing, so it can be the subject of a sentence and you can add more information to it.

You already do this in Indonesian with **ke-an** and **pe-an**: *memutuskan → keputusan, naik → kenaikan, tumbuh → pertumbuhan, kurang → kekurangan, sebab → penyebab*.

Quick recap from B1–B2: the endings **-tion/-sion, -ment, -ance/-ence, -ity, -ness** make nouns (*reduce → reduction, improve → improvement, perform → performance, able → ability, aware → awareness*). But many of the most useful nouns don't follow those endings, so learn them one by one:
- **same form as the verb**: *increase, decrease, rise, fall, change, demand, cause, delay, need, cut* (*prices rose → **a rise** in prices*)
- **-al**: *arrive → arrival, refuse → refusal, approve → approval*
- **-th**: *grow → growth, strong → strength, long → length*
- **a new form**: *fail → failure, analyse → analysis, die → death, lose → loss, choose → choice, believe → belief, consume → consumption*

id.text:
**Nominalisasi** artinya mengubah **kata kerja** (kata yang menyatakan tindakan: *decide, grow*) atau **kata sifat** (kata yang menjelaskan: *important, strong*) menjadi **kata benda** (kata untuk 'benda' atau hal): *decide → **the decision**, important → **the importance***. Idenya menjadi sebuah 'hal', sehingga bisa menjadi subjek kalimat dan bisa kamu tambahi informasi.

Kamu sudah melakukan ini dalam bahasa Indonesia dengan **ke-an** dan **pe-an**: *memutuskan → keputusan, naik → kenaikan, tumbuh → pertumbuhan, kurang → kekurangan, sebab → penyebab*.

Ulasan singkat dari B1–B2: akhiran **-tion/-sion, -ment, -ance/-ence, -ity, -ness** membentuk kata benda (*reduce → reduction, improve → improvement, perform → performance, able → ability, aware → awareness*). Tapi banyak kata benda yang paling berguna tidak memakai akhiran itu, jadi hafalkan satu per satu:
- **bentuknya sama dengan kata kerjanya**: *increase, decrease, rise, fall, change, demand, cause, delay, need, cut* (*prices rose → **a rise** in prices*)
- **-al**: *arrive → arrival, refuse → refusal, approve → approval*
- **-th**: *grow → growth, strong → strength, long → length*
- **bentuk baru**: *fail → failure, analyse → analysis, die → death, lose → loss, choose → choice, believe → belief, consume → consumption*

rows.en: The growth of digital banking has changed how young people save.
rows.id: Pertumbuhan perbankan digital telah mengubah cara anak muda menabung.

rows.en: Dr. Wulan explained the importance of sleep for memory.
rows.id: Dr. Wulan menjelaskan pentingnya tidur bagi daya ingat.

rows.en: The failure of the project cost the startup two billion rupiah.
rows.id: Kegagalan proyek itu membuat startup tersebut rugi dua miliar rupiah.

rows.en: There was a long delay in the delivery of the new laptops.
rows.id: Ada keterlambatan panjang dalam pengiriman laptop-laptop baru itu.
rows.note: delay: the same form as the verb

id.note: delay: bentuknya sama dengan kata kerjanya

rows.en: Their analysis of the survey data took two weeks.
rows.id: Analisis mereka terhadap data survei itu memakan waktu dua minggu.

blocks.text:
**Two traps.**
1) A verb can't come after *the*: *The decide to close the office was difficult* ✗ → ***The decision** to close the office was difficult.*
2) Don't make a noun with **-ing** when a normal noun exists: *The increasing of prices worries people* ✗ → ***The increase in** prices worries people.* (*the -ing of* is possible with a few verbs, but if a normal noun exists, such as *increase, decision, growth, analysis*, use it.)

Also: *penting → pentingnya* (*the importance of education* = pentingnya pendidikan). *Kepentingan* usually means *interest* (*kepentingan umum* = *the public interest*). And listen for the stress: the noun is ***IN**crease, **DE**crease*, the verb is *in**CREASE**, de**CREASE***.

id.text:
**Dua jebakan.**
1) Kata kerja tidak bisa langsung setelah *the*: *The decide to close the office was difficult* ✗ → ***The decision** to close the office was difficult.*
2) Jangan membuat kata benda dengan **-ing** kalau sudah ada kata benda yang biasa: *The increasing of prices worries people* ✗ → ***The increase in** prices worries people.* (*the -ing of* memang bisa dipakai untuk beberapa kata kerja, tapi kalau ada kata benda yang biasa, seperti *increase, decision, growth, analysis*, pakai itu.)

Satu lagi: *penting → pentingnya* (*the importance of education* = pentingnya pendidikan). *Kepentingan* biasanya berarti *interest* (*kepentingan umum* = *the public interest*). Perhatikan juga tekanannya: kata bendanya ***IN**crease, **DE**crease*, kata kerjanya *in**CREASE**, de**CREASE***.

blocks.prompt: Many students don't understand the ___ of a good CV.
blocks.explain: After *the* (and before *of*) you need a noun: **importance**. *important* is the adjective and *importantly* the adverb.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Many students don't understand the ___ of a good CV.
id.explain: Setelah *the* (dan sebelum *of*) kamu butuh kata benda: **importance**. *important* adalah kata sifat dan *importantly* kata keterangan.

blocks.text:
When a verb becomes a noun, the noun often needs **its own preposition** (kata depan), even if the verb had none: *Prices increased* → *an increase **in** prices*; *The rules affect small shops* → *the effect of the rules **on** small shops*. Learn each noun together with its preposition:
- **decision to / refusal to** + verb: *the decision to raise fees, their refusal to pay*
- **importance of, cause of, lack of**: *the cause of the delay, a lack of time*
- **increase / decrease / rise / fall / reduction / improvement in** + what changes: *a rise in fuel prices*. With the **amount**, use **of** (as in B2): *a rise of 10%*
- **solution to** + the problem: *a solution to the traffic problem*
- **demand for, need for, reason for**: *a demand for electric cars*
- **effect / impact of** X **on** Y: *the effect of social media on teenagers*

id.text:
Kalau kata kerja menjadi kata benda, kata bendanya sering butuh **kata depannya sendiri**, walaupun kata kerjanya tidak memakai kata depan: *Prices increased* → *an increase **in** prices*; *The rules affect small shops* → *the effect of the rules **on** small shops*. Hafalkan tiap kata benda bersama kata depannya:
- **decision to / refusal to** + kata kerja: *the decision to raise fees, their refusal to pay*
- **importance of, cause of, lack of**: *the cause of the delay, a lack of time*
- **increase / decrease / rise / fall / reduction / improvement in** + hal yang berubah: *a rise in fuel prices*. Untuk **jumlah** perubahannya, pakai **of** (seperti di B2): *a rise of 10%*
- **solution to** + masalahnya: *a solution to the traffic problem*
- **demand for, need for, reason for**: *a demand for electric cars*
- **effect / impact of** X **on** Y: *the effect of social media on teenagers*

rows.id: Keputusan untuk menaikkan biaya kuliah memicu protes mahasiswa.

rows.en: Experts disagree about the main cause of the floods.
rows.id: Para ahli tidak sepakat tentang penyebab utama banjir itu.

rows.en: Bike lanes are only part of the solution to the traffic problem.
rows.id: Jalur sepeda hanya sebagian dari solusi untuk masalah kemacetan.

rows.en: There has been a big fall in the number of cash payments.
rows.id: Ada penurunan besar dalam jumlah pembayaran tunai.

rows.en: The study looked at the effect of online classes on students' grades.
rows.id: Penelitian itu meneliti pengaruh kelas online terhadap nilai mahasiswa.

rows.en: Many villages still suffer from a lack of clean water.
rows.id: Banyak desa masih menderita karena kurangnya air bersih.

blocks.text:
**Indonesian traps.** Indonesian often has no preposition here (*kenaikan harga*), or uses *terhadap, untuk, akan*, which don't match English one to one:
- *kenaikan harga* → *a rise **in** prices* (not *a rise of prices* ✗)
- *dampak X terhadap Y* → *the effect of X **on** Y* (not *effect to* ✗)
- *permintaan akan* → *a demand **for***; *kurangnya* → *a lack **of***
- the **verb** *lack* has no preposition: *The team lacks experience* (not *lacks of* ✗). Only the noun takes *of*: *a lack of experience*.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia.** Bahasa Indonesia sering tidak memakai kata depan di sini (*kenaikan harga*), atau memakai *terhadap, untuk, akan*, yang tidak sama persis dengan bahasa Inggris:
- *kenaikan harga* → *a rise **in** prices* (bukan *a rise of prices* ✗)
- *dampak X terhadap Y* → *the effect of X **on** Y* (bukan *effect to* ✗)
- *permintaan akan* → *a demand **for***; *kurangnya* → *a lack **of***
- **kata kerja** *lack* tidak memakai kata depan: *The team lacks experience* (bukan *lacks of* ✗). Hanya kata bendanya yang memakai *of*: *a lack of experience*.

blocks.prompt: The city needs a long-term solution ___ the flooding problem.
blocks.explain: **a solution to** + the problem. *in* goes with change nouns (*an increase in*), and *at* doesn't go with *solution*.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The city needs a long-term solution ___ the flooding problem.
id.explain: **a solution to** + masalahnya. *in* dipakai dengan kata benda perubahan (*an increase in*), dan *at* tidak dipakai dengan *solution*.

id.title: Menyusun frasa kata benda yang kompleks

blocks.text:
A **noun phrase** is a group of words built around one main noun, the **head** (kata inti). In formal writing one noun phrase can carry a lot of information:
*a significant, unexpected **increase** in online sales*
*the rapid **growth** of e-commerce in Indonesia over the past five years*

- **Before** the head (pre-modifiers): articles, numbers, adjectives, and nouns used like adjectives: *a significant, unexpected …; **online** sales; a **five-year** plan*
- **After** the head (post-modifiers): phrases with a preposition (*in online sales, of e-commerce, in Indonesia*), time phrases (*over the past five years*) and relative clauses (*the plan that we discussed*)

The verb agrees with the **head**, not with the nearest noun: *The rapid growth of online shops **has** changed retail* (growth = one thing, so *has*).

id.text:
**Frasa kata benda** adalah sekelompok kata yang dibangun di sekitar satu kata benda utama, yaitu **kata inti** (head). Dalam tulisan formal, satu frasa kata benda bisa membawa banyak informasi:
*a significant, unexpected **increase** in online sales*
*the rapid **growth** of e-commerce in Indonesia over the past five years*

- **Sebelum** kata inti (pre-modifier): artikel, angka, kata sifat, dan kata benda yang berfungsi seperti kata sifat: *a significant, unexpected …; **online** sales; a **five-year** plan*
- **Sesudah** kata inti (post-modifier): frasa dengan kata depan (*in online sales, of e-commerce, in Indonesia*), keterangan waktu (*over the past five years*) dan anak kalimat relatif (*the plan that we discussed*)

Kata kerjanya mengikuti **kata inti**, bukan kata benda yang paling dekat: *The rapid growth of online shops **has** changed retail* (growth = satu hal, jadi *has*).

rows.en: an increase in online sales

rows.en: a significant increase in online sales

rows.en: The rapid growth of e-commerce in Indonesia over the past five years has changed how small shops work.
rows.id: Pertumbuhan pesat e-commerce di Indonesia selama lima tahun terakhir telah mengubah cara kerja toko-toko kecil.

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian order trap.** Indonesian puts the describing words **after** the main noun: *kenaikan penjualan online **yang signifikan***. English puts adjectives and describing nouns **before** it: *a **significant** increase in **online** sales* (not *an increase in online sales significant* ✗). The *in / of* phrases come after the head in both languages.

**Keep it readable.** Two or three modifiers around one head is plenty. If a phrase gets longer than that, split it into two sentences or use a verb.

id.text:
**Jebakan urutan bahasa Indonesia.** Bahasa Indonesia meletakkan kata penjelas **sesudah** kata benda utamanya: *kenaikan penjualan online **yang signifikan***. Bahasa Inggris meletakkan kata sifat dan kata benda penjelas **sebelum** kata inti: *a **significant** increase in **online** sales* (bukan *an increase in online sales significant* ✗). Frasa *in / of* tetap di belakang kata inti di kedua bahasa.

**Jaga supaya mudah dibaca.** Dua atau tiga kata penjelas di sekitar satu kata inti sudah cukup. Kalau frasanya lebih panjang dari itu, pecah jadi dua kalimat atau pakai kata kerja.

blocks.prompt: Which is the natural English for 'penggunaan media sosial yang berlebihan oleh remaja'?
options: the use excessive of social media by teenagers
the excessive use of social media by teenagers
the excessive use social media of teenagers
blocks.explain: Head = **use**. The adjective *excessive* goes **before** it, and the phrases *of social media* and *by teenagers* go after it. The first option keeps the Indonesian order; the third loses *of* after *use*.

id.prompt: Mana bahasa Inggris yang wajar untuk 'penggunaan media sosial yang berlebihan oleh remaja'?
id.explain: Kata intinya **use**. Kata sifat *excessive* diletakkan **sebelum** kata inti, dan frasa *of social media* serta *by teenagers* sesudahnya. Pilihan pertama masih memakai urutan bahasa Indonesia; pilihan ketiga kehilangan *of* setelah *use*.

id.title: Dari gaya sehari-hari ke gaya akademik

blocks.text:
Reports, essays and academic papers often turn a sentence about **people doing things** into a sentence built on **nouns**. Three steps:
1. Find the verb or adjective that carries the main idea (*rose, bought less*).
2. Turn it into a noun phrase. An **adverb** (kata keterangan: *quickly, sharply, slightly*) becomes an **adjective** before the noun: *rose quickly → **a rapid rise** in prices*, *fell sharply → **a sharp fall***.
3. Link the noun phrases with a verb that shows cause and effect: ***led to, caused, resulted in, was due to, was caused by***.

*Because prices rose quickly, people bought less.* → ***The rapid rise in prices led to a fall in consumption.***

The formal version has one clear subject, it's shorter, and it's about the facts, not about *people*: that's why reports and essays like it.

id.text:
Laporan, esai dan makalah akademik sering mengubah kalimat tentang **orang yang melakukan sesuatu** menjadi kalimat yang dibangun dari **kata benda**. Tiga langkah:
1. Cari kata kerja atau kata sifat yang membawa ide utama (*rose, bought less*).
2. Ubah menjadi frasa kata benda. **Kata keterangan** (*quickly, sharply, slightly*) berubah jadi **kata sifat** sebelum kata benda: *rose quickly → **a rapid rise** in prices*, *fell sharply → **a sharp fall***.
3. Hubungkan frasa-frasa kata benda itu dengan kata kerja yang menunjukkan sebab-akibat: ***led to, caused, resulted in, was due to, was caused by***.

*Because prices rose quickly, people bought less.* → ***The rapid rise in prices led to a fall in consumption.***

Versi formalnya punya satu subjek yang jelas, lebih ringkas, dan berbicara tentang fakta, bukan tentang *orang*: karena itu laporan dan esai menyukainya.

rows.en: Because prices rose quickly, people bought less.
rows.id: Karena harga naik dengan cepat, orang membeli lebih sedikit.

rows.en: The rapid rise in prices led to a fall in consumption.
rows.id: Kenaikan harga yang pesat menyebabkan penurunan konsumsi.

rows.en: The government decided to cut subsidies, and many people protested.
rows.id: Pemerintah memutuskan untuk memotong subsidi, dan banyak orang protes.

rows.en: The government's decision to cut subsidies resulted in widespread protests.
rows.id: Keputusan pemerintah untuk memotong subsidi mengakibatkan protes yang meluas.

rows.en: The air in Jakarta got worse because there were more and more cars.
rows.id: Udara di Jakarta makin buruk karena mobilnya makin banyak.

rows.en: The decline in air quality in Jakarta was caused by the growing number of cars.
rows.id: Penurunan kualitas udara di Jakarta disebabkan oleh jumlah mobil yang terus bertambah.

blocks.text: **Adverb → adjective.** When the verb becomes a noun, the adverb that described it becomes an adjective: *grew steadily → steady growth*, *fell slightly → a slight fall*. *a rapidly rise* ✗ is a common slip: before a noun, use the adjective.

id.text: **Kata keterangan → kata sifat.** Kalau kata kerjanya menjadi kata benda, kata keterangan yang menjelaskannya berubah jadi kata sifat: *grew steadily → steady growth*, *fell slightly → a slight fall*. *a rapidly rise* ✗ adalah kesalahan yang sering terjadi: sebelum kata benda, pakai kata sifat.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is the best choice for a formal report? Everyday version: 'More people now work from home, so offices use less electricity.'
options: The rising of working from home has caused the using of less electricity in offices.
More people working from home so offices using less electricity.
The rise in remote working has led to a fall in office electricity use.
blocks.explain: **The rise in remote working** (noun + in) **has led to** (cause-effect verb) **a fall in office electricity use**. The first option builds clumsy -ing nouns (*the rising of, the using of*) where real nouns exist; the second has no main verb.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang paling cocok untuk laporan formal? Versi sehari-hari: 'More people now work from home, so offices use less electricity.'
id.explain: **The rise in remote working** (kata benda + in) **has led to** (kata kerja sebab-akibat) **a fall in office electricity use**. Pilihan pertama membuat kata benda -ing yang janggal (*the rising of, the using of*) padahal ada kata benda yang sebenarnya; pilihan kedua tidak punya kata kerja utama.

blocks.text:
Nominalisation is a tool for reports, essays and academic papers, not a rule for every sentence. At C1 this is a **style choice**, and good writers use it carefully:
- **Too many nouns are hard to read.** *The implementation of a reduction in the use of plastic bags is the aim of this initiative.* → *This initiative aims to reduce the use of plastic bags.*
- **Nouns can hide who did it.** *A decision was made to cut the budget* (who decided?). When it matters, name the person: *The board decided to cut the budget.*
- **Emails, chats and speaking** normally use plain verbs: *We've moved the meeting to Thursday* is friendlier and clearer than *The relocation of the meeting to Thursday has been decided.*

A good rule: one or two noun phrases per sentence, and a real verb that does the work.

id.text:
Nominalisasi adalah alat untuk laporan, esai dan makalah akademik, bukan aturan untuk setiap kalimat. Di level C1 ini adalah **pilihan gaya**, dan penulis yang baik memakainya dengan hati-hati:
- **Terlalu banyak kata benda membuat tulisan sulit dibaca.** *The implementation of a reduction in the use of plastic bags is the aim of this initiative.* → *This initiative aims to reduce the use of plastic bags.*
- **Kata benda bisa menyembunyikan siapa pelakunya.** *A decision was made to cut the budget* (siapa yang memutuskan?). Kalau itu penting, sebutkan orangnya: *The board decided to cut the budget.*
- **Email, chat dan percakapan** biasanya memakai kata kerja yang sederhana: *We've moved the meeting to Thursday* lebih ramah dan jelas daripada *The relocation of the meeting to Thursday has been decided.*

Patokan yang baik: satu atau dua frasa kata benda per kalimat, dan satu kata kerja yang benar-benar bekerja.

rows.en: The implementation of a reduction in the use of plastic bags is the aim of this initiative.
rows.id: Pelaksanaan pengurangan penggunaan kantong plastik adalah tujuan inisiatif ini.

rows.en: This initiative aims to reduce the use of plastic bags.
rows.id: Inisiatif ini bertujuan mengurangi penggunaan kantong plastik.

rows.en: A decision was made to cut the budget.
rows.id: Diputuskan untuk memotong anggaran.

rows.en: The board decided to cut the budget.
rows.id: Dewan direksi memutuskan untuk memotong anggaran.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani is writing a quick email to her team about Friday's meeting. Which sentence fits best?
options: The relocation of Friday's meeting to Room 3 has been the subject of a decision.
We've moved Friday's meeting to Room 3.
Friday's meeting relocation to Room 3 decision.
blocks.explain: In a quick email to colleagues, a plain verb is clearer and friendlier: **We've moved …**. The first option piles up nouns for no reason, and the third isn't a sentence.

id.prompt: Bu Ani menulis email singkat kepada timnya tentang rapat hari Jumat. Kalimat mana yang paling cocok?
id.explain: Dalam email singkat kepada rekan kerja, kata kerja yang sederhana lebih jelas dan ramah: **We've moved …**. Pilihan pertama menumpuk kata benda tanpa alasan, dan pilihan ketiga bukan kalimat.

id.intro: Selamat datang di C1! Bahasa Inggris akademik dan bahasa laporan sering menyampaikan sesuatu dengan kata benda, bukan kata kerja: bukan 'prices rose quickly', tapi 'the rapid rise in prices'. Di pelajaran ini kamu mengubah kata kerja dan kata sifat menjadi kata benda, menambahkan kata depan yang tepat sesudahnya, menyusun frasa kata benda yang lebih panjang, dan belajar kapan gaya ini membantu dan kapan justru membuat tulisanmu berat.

assessment.nm-1: Lengkapi dengan bentuk kata benda dari kata dalam kurung: The ___ (strong) of the rupiah against the US dollar last month helped many importers.
assessment.nm-2: Lengkapi dengan bentuk kata benda dari kata kerja dalam kurung DAN kata yang mengikutinya (dua kata): The company's ___ ___ (refuse) pay overtime led to a three-day strike.
assessment.nm-3: Tulis kata depan yang hilang: The ministry's report shows a sharp increase ___ the number of electric motorbikes in Jakarta.
assessment.nm-4: Tulis frasa kata benda ini dalam bahasa Inggris, memakai kata sharp, rise dan cost of living: kenaikan biaya hidup yang tajam
assessment.nm-5: Temukan dan perbaiki kesalahan dalam kalimat dari sebuah laporan ini: The number of applications from Surabaya have doubled since last year.
assessment.nm-6: Buat kalimat ini formal. Lengkapi bagian kosong dengan frasa kata benda (4–5 kata) berdasarkan kalimat pertama. Sehari-hari: 'Sales fell slightly in March.' Formal: 'There was ___ in March.'
assessment.nm-7: Buat kalimat ini formal dengan melengkapi bagian kosong memakai satu kata benda (dalam bahasa Inggris). Sehari-hari: 'Lots of customers complained, so we changed the app.' Formal: 'The large number of customer ___ led to changes in the app.'
